note: Two games stalled because the route map promised routes that only work from one exact pixel. Each platform cell was valued as if the player stood at its centre, so jumps that need a pixel-perfect start (a gap between two ledges exactly one player-width wide on the level-2 map) or a near-apex corner landing (the tiny top platform on level 1) kept showing the best eta. In seed 101 at 53 ms the player jumped in place under a ledge for 10 s, and in seed 202 at 53 ms it bumped its head under the top platform for 40 s. Changes, kept small and general: (1) a jump edge enters the route map only if the same jump also reaches the same platform level when started 5 px to the left and right of the cell centre; (2) a corner step-up now needs the vertical overlap to be smaller than the sideways overlap, as Phaser resolves it; (3) while a coin is overdue, the cell the player keeps standing on gets a growing cost (the earlier penalty idea, without the enemy-jump 'sure' mode that played worse on unseen seeds). The teacher and its rules are unchanged.
instructions:
Super Coin Box: run (Left/Right) and jump (Up) to grab the coin; a new one appears elsewhere each time. Enemies drop in through the top centre: landing on one from above kills it, any other touch costs a life, and so does falling out through the hole in the floor (3 lives). Collect as many coins as possible.
Forecast fields: ifIdle, ifLeft, ifRight, ifJump, ifJumpLeft, ifJumpRight each simulate choosing that action now. The keys in force now (the current running direction) stay in force until the input lands: the measured input delay rounded up to whole frames, plus the one frame the game takes to turn a key into motion (only that one frame when the game waits for every decision). Then the action is held for 0.1 s, followed by the best of a set of simple follow-up moves. The simulation uses the level map, every enemy's predicted path and the next enemy drop predicted from the spawn rhythm, for about 1.4 s. A corner landing counts only when the body sinks into the ledge less than it overlaps it sideways. safe = true: some follow-up keeps a margin from every enemy (3 px when the game waits for decisions, 4 px in real time) or stomps it from above, and avoids the floor hole and the top of the world; in real time the action must also survive its input landing one frame later. eta = predicted seconds until the coin is touched. Below 50: a known route. The route map keeps a jump only if it reaches the same platform level from the cell centre and from 5 px to either side, so routes that need a pixel-exact start are left out. A jump straight up counts only from spots where a simulated jump touches the coin without hitting a ceiling, plus the walk to such a spot. 50 to 75: no route known, smaller = closer. 99: no coin or nothing safe. While the coin is overdue, the cell the player stands on gets an extra cost that grows with the time spent there (up to 8 s). That cost is added to every route or coin touch that starts from it, so a route that keeps failing gives way to others. On the ground with no enemy within 200 px, ifIdle.eta is at least 0.1 larger than the smallest eta of the other actions (standing still only delays). hitIn = seconds until contact for an action that is not safe (9 when safe). coinOverdue = true when the current coin has stayed uncollected more than 2.5 s longer than first predicted. coinEta = the smallest eta among the safe actions, leaving idle out when coinOverdue is true (99 when there is none). fast = true when the action is safe, its eta is at most coinEta + 0.01 (it ties the best), and it is not idle while coinOverdue is true. runningRight / runningLeft = true when the player is running that way right now (the keys in force); both are false when the player is not running.
Rules: 1) If playing is false (between lives, level change, game over), choose jump or click, 50/50. 2) Otherwise take the actions whose fast is true. If runningRight is true and at least one of them runs right (right or jumpRight), keep only those. If runningLeft is true and at least one of them runs left (left or jumpLeft), keep only those. If one action remains, choose it; otherwise split the probability equally among the remaining actions. 3) If no action is fast but ifIdle.safe is true (only possible when coinOverdue is true), choose idle. 4) If no action is safe, choose the action with the largest hitIn; on a tie the smaller eta; split equally among the actions still tied. 5) If the ifX fields are missing, go right when coinDx > 10, left when coinDx < -10, otherwise idle.
Context only: enemies = the 3 nearest threats (dx, dy from the player, positive dy = below; vx, vy), onGround (a player resting up to 4 px above a floor counts as on it), pitBelow, coinDx/coinDy, graphReady = the route map is complete.

actions.description: release all keys: stand still, or drop straight down when airborne
jump straight up (Up held; jumps again on landing)
jump while running left (Up held; jumps again on landing)
jump while running right (Up held; jumps again on landing)
click the game centre (start or restart screens)

tests.why: The extractor must run without throwing on real frames, including coin pickups (the player hitbox briefly grows), a level-2 map, a life lost and the end screen.
Whenever the player is in play, the per-action forecasts, coinEta and coinOverdue must be present, because the teacher's rules read them.

tests.expect: !(state.playing && state.onGround && state.graphReady && state.ifIdle && state.ifIdle.safe && state.coinEta > 0.3 && state.coinEta < 50 && (state.enemies || []).every(function (e) { return Math.abs(e.dx) + Math.abs(e.dy) > 220; })) || state.ifIdle.eta > Math.min(state.ifLeft.eta, state.ifRight.eta, state.ifJump.eta, state.ifJumpLeft.eta, state.ifJumpRight.eta) + 0.04
tests.why: Pins the stall fix. On the ground, with a known route and no enemy nearby, waiting must cost more than the 0.04 tie margin. The previous attempt scored route distance on every grounded frame, so idle was within 0.02 of moving and the player stood still for whole games.
The extractor must run without throwing on the seed-202 ending: the player sprite enlarged against the right wall, predicted enemy drops, and a life lost.
The extractor must run without throwing on the seed-303 ending: an enemy walking into the player on a platform, then the end screen.
The extractor must run without throwing on the level-2 map and a fresh spawn falling on the player.

tests.expect: !state.playing || !state.ifIdle || ['ifIdle','ifLeft','ifRight','ifJump','ifJumpLeft','ifJumpRight'].every(function (k) { var o = state[k]; return !!o && typeof o.fast === 'boolean' && (!o.fast || (o.safe === true && o.eta <= state.coinEta + 0.041)) && !(k === 'ifIdle' && o.fast && state.coinOverdue); })
tests.why: The teacher chooses the first action with fast = true, so fast must mean: safe, within 0.04 of coinEta, and never idle while coinOverdue is true.
Whenever any moving action is safe, at least one action must be fast; otherwise the teacher would fall through to the hitIn fallback while a safe move exists.

tests.expect: state.score === undefined && state.lives === undefined && state.message === undefined
tests.why: Score, lives and the level text only change as the game goes on and no rule uses them, so they stay out of the state: otherwise the model would act on when it is rather than on the situation.

The extractor must not throw on the kept profile's seed-303 ending (a jump at the floor's edge, the fall into the hole, the end screen). This covers the new jump-goal simulation and the resting-player snap.
The same no-throw check on the kept profile's seed-101 ending (crowded floor, enemy contact, a life lost).
The new tie rule reads the running direction. It must be present whenever the player is in play, as two booleans that are never both true.
No state field may carry an action id as its value, because such fields are stripped as advice. The running direction is therefore two booleans, not 'left'/'right'.

tests.expect: !state.playing || !state.ifIdle || ['ifIdle','ifLeft','ifRight','ifJump','ifJumpLeft','ifJumpRight'].every(function (k) { var o = state[k]; return !o.fast || (o.safe === true && o.eta <= state.coinEta + 0.011); })
tests.why: Pins the tight tie: fast means within 0.01 of the best eta. The keep-direction rule then only chooses among actions that are truly equal, never between a slower one and a faster one.

tests.why: Waiting on calm ground must still cost more than the tie margin now that a player resting up to 4 px above a floor counts as on the ground.

tests.why: With the overdue cell penalty folded into the etas, fast must still mean: safe, tied with coinEta within 0.01, and never idle while the coin is overdue.
Penalised routes must never leave the teacher without a fast action while some moving action is safe; otherwise it falls through to the hitIn fallback.
